purpose: The cross-repo pin for the unaimed-placement lattice: hermes `agent_runtime/office_layout_policy.py` and the launcher's `MissionOfficePlacementPolicy` must resolve every case below to the same slot within 1e-4. Hand-maintained; see README.md for the update rule.

cases.name: empty_floor
cases.why: Nothing placed yet: the first unaimed agent lands on the WORLD ORIGIN (operator ruling 2026-08-27), not on a viewport guess and not on the old canvas drop band.

cases.name: occupied_origin_steps_up_one_full_row
cases.why: THE ruling, as a case: the origin is taken, so the next placement stands one FULL grid step above it — never beside it. A policy that stepped sideways here would satisfy every other case in this file.

cases.name: gap_is_filled_not_appended
cases.why: Rows 0 and 2 of column 0 taken: the scan fills the HOLE at row 1 rather than appending past the end, which is what makes it deterministic under removal.

cases.name: full_first_column_wraps
cases.why: All eight rows of column 0 taken: the next slot wraps SIDEWAYS to column 1 row 0 instead of climbing off the top of the floor.

cases.name: hidden_item_blocks
cases.why: A hidden item keeps its coordinates and can be un-hidden at any time, so it occupies its slot. `hidden` is launcher-only; hermes passes this by never having had the field.

cases.name: other_folder_does_not_block
cases.why: The scan is folder-scoped: a desk sitting on the agent origin does not push an agent off it.

cases.name: blank_folder_falls_back_to_kind
cases.why: hermes persists `folder: ""` for an item written without one and the launcher substitutes the kind default at decode. Both must treat this agent as being in Agents, or a legacy item blocks on one repo and is invisible on the other.

cases.name: blank_folder_desk_falls_back_to_desks
cases.why: The same fallback on the desk lane: a blank-foldered desk occupies the DESK lattice, not the agent one.

cases.name: desk_lane_offset
cases.why: Desks scan their own lane, offset diagonally off the agent lattice, so the first unaimed desk and the first unaimed agent never stack on one point.

cases.name: desk_lane_second_desk
cases.why: A second unaimed desk climbs its own lane by one full row, the same rule the agent lane follows.

cases.name: off_lattice_item_blocks_its_nearest_slot
cases.why: An item dropped between lattice points blocks the slot it is NEAREST, so a hand-placed agent still pushes the next unaimed one up a step.

cases.name: boundary_item_at_exact_radius
cases.why: The ONE case whose verdict turns on the occupancy comparison. The x offset is 1468007 * 2**-21 = 0.700000286102294921875 — the nearest float32-representable point at or outside occupancy_radius. Spelled the obvious way (slot + 0.7) the two repos DISAGREE even at the world origin: the launcher stores 0.7 into a float32 Vector2 as 0.69999998807907104 and compares it against a float64 occupancyRadius of 0.7, so the item blocks there and stays free on hermes. Only Vector2 STORAGE is 32-bit; the constant is not. Measured 2026-08-27.

cases.name: pigeonhole_200_occupied
cases.why: The termination bound, exercised: 25 full columns are taken, so the scan must return the first slot of column 25 rather than a knowingly-occupied point.
